src/experiments/compare_epochs.py.help:
usage: compare_epochs.py [-h] --arch ARCH --epoch-1 EPOCH_1 --epoch-2 EPOCH_2
                         [--epoch-3 EPOCH_3] [--base BASE]
                         [--out-epoch OUT_EPOCH]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --arch ARCH
  --epoch-1 EPOCH_1     epoch-1 pure-FT eval json
  --epoch-2 EPOCH_2     epoch-2 pure-FT eval json
  --epoch-3 EPOCH_3     epoch-3 result, v5 validation results only
  --base BASE           the shared base-checkpoint eval json
  --out-epoch OUT_EPOCH

src/experiments/eval_finetune.py.help:
usage: eval_finetune.py [-h] [--adapter ADAPTER] --tag TAG [--dry-run]
                        [--base-model BASE_MODEL] [--revision REVISION]
                        [--only-set ONLY_SET] [--result-epoch RESULT_EPOCH]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --adapter ADAPTER     path to lora adapter dir, empty = base model
  --tag TAG             label for the output json, e.g. base / finetuned
  --dry-run             load eval sets only, no model
  --base-model BASE_MODEL
                        hf checkpoint to evaluate when no --adapter is given
  --revision REVISION   exact hf revision of --base-model
  --only-set ONLY_SET   evaluate a single named set (e.g.
                        robustness_holdout_v2), for cheap re-evals of already-
                        scored checkpoints on a new set
  --result-epoch RESULT_EPOCH
                        which epoch-N report tree to write raw results into;
                        the evaluation sets themselves are frozen and
                        identical across epochs

src/experiments/finetune_lora.py.help:
usage: finetune_lora.py [-h] [--smoke] [--subsample SUBSAMPLE]
                        [--batch-size BATCH_SIZE] [--grad-accum GRAD_ACCUM]
                        [--max-seq-length MAX_SEQ_LENGTH]
                        [--train-jsonl TRAIN_JSONL]
                        [--dataset {reverse_auction,sealed,v5_reverse_auction,v5_sealed,v5_supervisor}]
                        [--num-train-epochs NUM_TRAIN_EPOCHS]
                        [--max-steps MAX_STEPS] [--include-edge]
                        [--edge-repeat EDGE_REPEAT]
                        [--edge-weights EDGE_WEIGHTS]
                        [--output-dir OUTPUT_DIR] [--base-model BASE_MODEL]
                        [--revision REVISION] [--edge-dir EDGE_DIR]
                        [--instruction-part INSTRUCTION_PART]
                        [--response-part RESPONSE_PART]
                        [--lora-targets LORA_TARGETS]
                        [--save-steps SAVE_STEPS] [--resume]
                        [--template-kwargs TEMPLATE_KWARGS] [--optim OPTIM]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --smoke               pipeline check: 48 examples, 8 steps
  --subsample SUBSAMPLE
                        train on the first N examples of the seeded shuffle
                        instead of all
  --batch-size BATCH_SIZE
  --grad-accum GRAD_ACCUM
  --max-seq-length MAX_SEQ_LENGTH
                        training sequence window. protocol v2 froze this at
                        1024 for the stage agents; the supervisor needs 2048
                        because a 12-candidate chain-selection prompt runs
                        ~1600 tokens
  --train-jsonl TRAIN_JSONL
                        train on this jsonl instead of the three stage files
                        (used for the supervisor set); --subsample/--include-
                        edge do not apply to it
  --dataset {reverse_auction,sealed,v5_reverse_auction,v5_sealed,v5_supervisor}
                        named training set: sealed is the round-1 stage data,
                        reverse_auction is the round 2/3 data; ignored with
                        --train-jsonl
  --num-train-epochs NUM_TRAIN_EPOCHS
                        passes over the training set (protocol v2 froze this
                        at 1; the epoch-2 family raises it to 2). the linear
                        LR schedule spans the WHOLE run, so N epochs is not
                        N-1 epochs plus one more -- the optimization
                        trajectory differs throughout
  --max-steps MAX_STEPS
                        stop after N steps for timing, extrapolate, save
                        nothing
  --include-edge        mix the synthetic edge training subset into the set
  --edge-repeat EDGE_REPEAT
                        repeat the edge training subset this many times (with
                        --include-edge)
  --edge-weights EDGE_WEIGHTS
                        per-category repeat overrides, e.g.
                        tailoring:boundary_infeasible=4, others keep --edge-
                        repeat
  --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        checkpoint and adapter output dir, use a fresh path
                        per round
  --base-model BASE_MODEL
                        hf checkpoint to fine-tune (frozen protocol: pin with
                        --revision)
  --revision REVISION   exact hf revision of --base-model
  --edge-dir EDGE_DIR   directory with edge_{stage}_train.jsonl, default data
                        dir; the round-one files live in
                        data/finetune/v4/round1_edge
  --instruction-part INSTRUCTION_PART
                        template marker before user turns (model-specific)
  --response-part RESPONSE_PART
                        template marker before assistant turns, loss starts
                        after it
  --lora-targets LORA_TARGETS
                        comma-separated LoRA target module names; use the
                        functionally-equivalent fused names for models like
                        phi (qkv_proj,o_proj,gate_up_proj,down_proj)
  --save-steps SAVE_STEPS
                        save a recovery checkpoint every N steps (0=off); does
                        not alter training math, only lets a crashed run
                        resume with --resume
  --resume              resume from the last checkpoint in --output-dir if one
                        exists
  --template-kwargs TEMPLATE_KWARGS
                        JSON kwargs for apply_chat_template during training
                        render, e.g. '{"enable_thinking": false}' for models
                        whose non-thinking mode is template-controlled
                        (smollm3); empty = prior behavior, all completed model
                        pipelines unchanged
  --optim OPTIM         trainer optimizer; adamw_8bit (bitsandbytes) is every
                        completed run's setting, adamw_torch is the fallback
                        where bitsandbytes is unavailable
